title: FAB Meeting Minutes - 4 August 2026
location: South Stand Meeting Room, Oakwell Stadium
content_text:
Barnsley FC Fan Advisory Board (FAB) 
Meeting Minutes 
Meeting held: Tuesday 4 August 2026, 6.15pm, South Stand Meeting Room, Oakwell Stadium 
A note on this record 
The meeting was recorded on a single room microphone, with two attendees (Lewis Robinson and Darren Hayes) 
joining by phone. Individual contributions from the club's staff have therefore been attributed by role (Chief 
Executive Officer, Head of Ticketing and Fan Engagement, and so on) rather than by name where the recording 
does not make clear which of them was speaking. FAB members are named where they identified 
themselves.This record follows the order of the published agenda. 
A guest session with the Head Coach took place before the formal agenda items and is recorded first, below. 
Attendees 
Present — Club representatives 
• Jon Flatman, Chief Executive Officer. 
• John Bird, Head of Ticketing and Fan Engagement. 
• Lewis Robinson, Club Press Officer (joined by phone). 
• Daniel Stendel, Head Coach, attended for an initial guest session only. 
• Darren Hayes, club commercial representative, joined by phone from the car with Lewis Robinson while 
travelling back from a meeting elsewhere. 
Present — Fan Advisory Board members 
• Steve Brain, Chair — Season Ticket Holder Representative. 
• Phil Hall — Diversity and Inclusion, and Barnsley FC Community Trust. 
• Martin Wilson — Disabled Supporters Representative. 
• Robin Harris — Youth and Children's Representative. 
• Alan Bloore — Supporters' Trust Representative. 
• Dominic Wood — Sponsors and Hospitality Representative. 
• Paul Gallagher — Supporters' Trust Representative 
• Peter — Fans Living away Representative. 
• Claire Calton — Women and Girls’ representative. 
Apologies: none recorded. 
Absent: none identified as expected but not in attendance. 
Quorum: the meeting was quorate. 
Guest Session: Head Coach Update 
Head Coach Daniel Stendel, back at the club for a second spell, joined for roughly the first half hour to answer 
questions from the Board. This was not a numbered item on the published agenda. 
The FAB welcomed DS back with a greeting, which was communicated in German: 
“Welcome back Daniel!! 
Speaking on behalf of the ten thousand fans who turn up here every other week, it’s a pleasure and a privilege to 
be able to say that you’re, once again, in charge of what happens on the grass. 
With your infectious, passionate and positive approach you have previously given us many golden memories. We 
now hope you can do the same again!! 
People say “It’s the hope that kills you.” In our case, the hope that you provide is enough to get us cheering again. 
Get in Daniel!! Allez les Rouges!! Vamos Rojos!! Auf gehts ihr Roten!! 
Come On You Reds!!’ 
DS said a lot had changed at the club since he left, on the Board and among staff, and that his priority was 
bringing back a sense of passion and belief. He was clear he did not see it as one person's job to turn things 
around. 
On the squad, he said he was pleased with pre-season progress but urged patience, pointing out the team could 
not be expected to “do everything from the first day.” He praised the performance and attitude shown in the 
recent friendly against Lincoln City and advised that Sam Gale for had signed only the Friday before, had not yet 
trained with the squad, and still started and played well, staying on longer than planned, through cramp, after 
another player was sent off. He said building team spirit was important and that regular Wednesday bonding 
sessions had been part of the response. Asked how he was settling new signings into an existing group, he said 
the quickest way to bring a squad together is winning matches, though results cannot simply be forced while the 
group beds in. 
Asked about connecting players with supporters, he referenced an unplanned moment where, after the Lincoln 
game, led by Cameron McGeehan, the squad went over to the East Stand for selfies and autographs with fans. 
He said he was keen to see more of that kind of thing happen, adding that the club was not “25 players, or John, 
or me” but everyone together. He asked supporters to keep expectations realistic while the squad settles, saying 
he could promise effort and commitment at all times. 
The Chair then gave Daniel Stendel a brief explanation of what the FAB is and does. The Board members then 
introduced themselves and the fan group each represents. DS thanked the Board and left the meeting at this 
point, advising that he would be happy to attend again if invited. 
1. Welcome 
The Chair opened the meeting and welcomed those present. 
2. Previous Minutes 
The Chair noted that most items from the previous minutes had either been resolved or were covered elsewhere 
on this month's agenda. One outstanding item, reports of bird droppings under the East Stand, was checked by a 
FAB member on a recent visit and not found to be a current problem, particularly now that the stand is open on 
matchdays. No further comments were raised and the previous minutes were taken as read. 
The Chair also noted it was good to be meeting again after a two to three month gap over the close season. 
3. IFR Update 
Paul Gallagher raised, ahead of the discussion, that the Independent Football Regulator (IFR)'s licensing 
guidance, which also sets out how Fan Advisory Boards like this one should be governed, had been published on 
1 July. 
The CEO said his early impression was that little of substance had changed from the club's perspective. This 
assessment is addressed separately, in the Any Other Business section below, where PG's own detailed 
comparison of the final guidance is recorded. The club's early impression proved to be broadly correct. 
The CEO then reported there was nothing further materially new to add since the last meeting, and talked 
through developments since the Football Governance Act came into force: 
• Where there is discretion for clubs, the guidance continues to focus on outcomes rather than mandating a 
fixed process. 
• There has been no formal communication yet from the IFR on next steps specifically for fan advisory 
groups. The IFR is not expected to engage directly with FABs, outside of clubs subject to a takeover, before 
around November. 
• The Regulator is heavily engaged in Owners, Directors and Senior Executive (ODSE) tests. Any change of 
ownership, club badge, name or colours is now live within the IFR's process, but none of this currently 
applies to Barnsley, as there has been no change of ownership. 
• One acknowledged change since the provisional guidance: the turnaround time for assessing a new 
appointment (for example, a new Chief Executive or Director) has been shortened considerably, after clubs 
raised concerns that the original timescale, combined with typical notice periods, could leave a post 
unfilled for the best part of a year. 
• The IFR has appointed a named club contact, and the club is supplying information as requested, as it 
always has done, though the Regulator now has statutory power to request it. 
• The CEO expects to be asked to submit a fan engagement plan once the IFR issues a template, alongside an 
outline of the club's approach. 
• The IFR is also involved in the wider, publicly reported discussions on a new financial distribution deal 
between the Premier League, EFL and the Regulator. Formal proposals are expected within the coming 
months and would need to go to a vote, but there is no guarantee a deal will be reached. 
AB suggested the Prime Minister, known to be a supporter of Everton, was likely to take a closer personal 
interest in how these discussions develop given his own affinity for the game. The CEO said he expected there 
would be ministerial interest but had no further detail to add. 
No questions were left unanswered on this item. 
4. Companies House Filings 
A supporter (ex FAB Member, Curtis Ledger) raised a query, on the public record, about how the club's ownership 
structure appears in Companies House Filings, specifically why a Hong Kong-registered holding company appears 
to show the full shareholding rather than reflecting an individual's percentage. 
The CEO advised that the Club's Finance Director, Rob Zuk, would contact Curtis directly to discuss the query 
further, given the technical nature of the question. 
Outcome: Rob Zuk will contact Curtis Ledger by phone to discuss the filing directly. A report on the outcome of 
that discussion will be brought back to the FAB and recorded in a future set of minutes. 
5. Fans' Questions 
Several supporter questions submitted in advance were worked through by the FAB, covering home friendlies, kit 
supplies, hotel discounts, car parking, new offices and the fanzone. 
Home Friendlies and Opposition 
A supporter had asked why home friendlies feature clubs such as Lincoln rather than bigger names. The CEO 
explained that pre-season fixtures build in difficulty through the summer, that Premier League and 
Championship sides are frequently touring or contractually committed elsewhere (including in World Cup years, 
when the calendar is further squeezed), and that the club has no automatic right to secure a marquee opponent. 
He also pointed out the pitch is unavailable for much of pre-season because it is re-laid annually, which limits 
home fixtures generally, and that many clubs in a similar position play the majority of their friendlies away. 
Several Board Members used this as a way into a related, recurring request: a fan-facing pre-season tour abroad, 
referencing previous trips under Daniel Stendel's first spell and the sense of togetherness it created. The CEO 
acknowledged the appeal but said the financial cost, and the logistical difficulty of fitting a tour around player 
recruitment (an early tour risks missing new signings entirely, as happened this summer with several recent 
arrivals), made it a genuinely difficult trade-off rather than a simple yes or no. He would not commit to a tour, 
but said the club would look at the idea properly before Christmas, in good time to plan for a future season if it 
goes ahead, rather than leaving a decision until the last minute. 
Kit Supplies 
A supporter asked why the away kit's training range was released later than the away match kit, when the two 
had come out together for the home kit. Club staff did not have full detail to hand but confirmed the training kit 
is now available, while the travel kit has yet to go on sale, with a date to be confirmed. It was also confirmed the 
third kit is expected to go on sale in late September or early October, in line with when the club expects to 
actually wear it, rather than all three kits launching together. FAB Members praised how the new goalkeeper kit 
launch had been timed to coincide with a new signing's unveiling, calling it well judged and well received by 
supporters. 
Hotel Discounts 
A question was raised about the visibility of hotel discounts for travelling supporters. JB advised that these are 
now listed on the club website under travelling/visiting fans information but must be booked by phone rather 
than online. Board Members felt this could be promoted more widely, for example through email newsletters, 
and it was noted the previous commercial contact who managed the scheme has left the hotel, with club 
arranging a meeting with the replacement to maintain the relationship. 
Car Parking 
A supporter question asked how many complaints the club receives about car parking, how those complaints are 
handled, and whether fans should expect to be held in the car parks for up to an hour after the final whistle. The 
CEO said this was a recurring topic covered in previous minutes and confirmed there are no new changes to 
report. 
He gave a detailed explanation of the reasoning behind the current arrangements. Parking and road closure rules 
are not set by the club acting alone: they sit within a legal safety framework agreed with the Safety Advisory 
Group, made up of the police, the ambulance service, the council and other local services, and any changes to 
those rules are discussed with the club in advance. He noted the club is fortunate to have a large amount of car 
parking close to the ground compared with many other clubs, but that this benefit comes with a trade-off, the 
road closures needed to manage it. He raised the growing national concern around vehicles being deliberately 
driven into crowds, and said that while the closures are inconvenient, they exist to protect the much larger 
number of supporters who arrive on foot. 
On the geography, he explained that every exit from the stadium's car parks funnels onto Pontefract Road, which 
is not something the club can change, and that this is comparable in principle to the layout challenges faced by 
other clubs' grounds, all of which have their own constraints. He said the current typical wait to be released from 
the car parks is in the region of up to 20 minutes; one FAB Member recalled the figure being closer to 20 minutes 
the previous season. The main cause of delay is that cars cannot be released until supporters on foot, many of 
whom walk up Grove Street, have cleared the area nearest the stadium, since pedestrian safety takes priority. 
He also disclosed that two of the club's traffic management staff were physically attacked last year while trying to 
stop people driving through closed sections, which he described as an unfortunate reflection of the pressures 
traffic and parking staff are under. A supporter's concern about new housing being built on Grove Street 
potentially adding to congestion was also raised; it was noted that residents in the nearby Oldfield area were 
previously offered a paid residents' parking permit scheme, priced at roughly £20 a year, which was not taken up. 
No changes to the current arrangements are planned. FAB Members accepted this was a clear and thorough 
explanation, if not the answer some fans want to hear. 
New Offices 
A supporter question challenged spending on new office space given the tight football budget. The CEO 
explained that the funding is a ring-fenced Council Capital Grant; part of a package of capital expenditure agreed 
with the Council as part of the Club's new lease roughly three and a half years ago, which cannot legally be 
redirected into football spending. He said the previous office environment was not fit for purpose for staff, 
players, sponsors or supporters, and that presenting a professional environment is directly tied to the Club's 
ability to raise commercial revenue and recruit players. He specifically highlighted the importance of first 
impressions when bringing players and player agents into the building during transfer discussions, saying the 
Club should not be negotiating deals in a space that looked tired or run down. FAB Members present did not 
dispute the need for the improvement, though it was acknowledged this had come up before as a source of 
confusion among fans about where the money had come from. 
Fanzone 
Progress on a permanent or semi-permanent fanzone was raised again. The CEO said further costings had been 
obtained since the last meeting for a smaller, more affordable structure, but stressed that the groundworks 
(power supply and security) are the main cost driver, not the structure itself, and a full roofed, year-round 
Fanzone remains expensive. The likely direction is a temporary, warm-months fanzone that could be expanded 
over time. The CEO said the harder question is not the physical space but what actually happens inside it for two 
hours on a matchday, and that he has asked staff to present a full business case, including running costs and 
expected food and drink sales, rather than just a design concept, so it can be weighed fairly against other 
potential uses of the same budget. 
6. Auracast Update 
PH gave an update on options for supporting visually impaired and hard-of-hearing supporters using Auracast, 
the broadcast audio technology that allows compatible hearing aids and receivers to pick up a live audio feed 
around the stadium. A supplier had quoted around £44,000 to install a system using 16 transmitters, which the 
Club considers excessive. FAB Members pointed to Cambridge United and Crystal Palace, who have run 
comparable systems with far fewer transmitters (one per stand) at a fraction of the cost, reportedly closer to 
£7,000 in Cambridge United's case, with receivers priced far below the roughly £329 per unit quoted to Barnsley. 
The Club agreed to investigate further and seek a contact at Cambridge United for a comparison. A FAB Member 
also described a lower-cost personal amplifier used at home, which some felt might offer a cheaper interim 
solution. 
Action: MW agreed to bring a personal receiver to Saturday's match and test its range around the ground, 
reporting back on how far the signal reaches. The existing hospital radio commentary service for visually 
impaired supporters will continue regardless of the outcome. 
7. DX Corner Stand — Top Floor (listed on the agenda as “Legends Suite”) 
This was the most heavily discussed item of the meeting. Although listed on the agenda as “Legends Suite,” the 
Chair initially introduced the item under that name before it was clarified during discussion that the area actually 
affected is the top floor of the Corner Stand, a distinct hospitality area, not the Legends Suite itself. The 
correction is noted here for accuracy; the outcome and actions arising from this item should be read as relating 
to the DX Corner Stand's top floor. 
Background given by the club: 
A hospitality sponsorship arrangement with Rapid Response Telecoms, a long-standing supporter of the club, has 
resulted in the Sponsor taking over the entire top floor of the DX Corner Stand, a hospitality area rather than a 
general seating tier, for staff and client use, in exchange for increased commercial revenue to the club. As part of 
this, existing season ticket holders on the DX Corner Stand's top floor were asked to relocate, either upwards to 
the Legends Suite or the 1887 Suite, where most were offered a substantial discount, understood to be in the 
region of 30%, or downwards to the Patrick's suite level, where no equivalent discount was offered. 
Concerns raised by FAB members, in particular by PG, who declared a personal conflict of interest as one of 
those affected: 
• Fans moved down to the Patrick's level were not offered an equivalent discount, and because ticket prices 
had risen for the new season generally, several of those fans are now paying more than they did last year 
for what most regard as a less desirable location, effectively paying more to move somewhere they did not 
want to go. 
• PG was clear that he accepted the club could not reasonably turn down a sponsorship of this scale from 
Rapid Response Telecoms. His point was about execution: a genuinely customer-focused approach would 
have ensured a discount for everyone affected by the move, not only those who relocated to the Legends 
Suite or 1887. 
• A change of this scale affecting existing season ticket holders was not brought to the FAB before it was 
finalised, which some members felt was comparable in principle to the earlier closure of the West Stand, 
an issue that had previously been discussed at this Board. 
• PG also noted that the FAB's Representative for this area of the fan base, Dominic Wood, whose portfolio 
covers sponsors and hospitality, had not communicated with him or, as far as he was aware, other affected 
fans ahead of time, and had not represented their interests in this instance. 
• The manner of communication, while conducted by personal phone call rather than by email, left some 
fans feeling they had not been treated fairly compared to those offered a discount. 
The Club's response: 
• The CEO said the Club had deliberately chosen to contact every affected supporter individually by phone 
rather than by a general email, and that this was a considered decision, not something rushed through 
without thought. 
• He acknowledged that the decision itself was never formally brought to the FAB, and said this had not been 
a conscious choice to exclude the Board, but that with hindsight it is the kind of decision that could and 
probably should come to this group in future. 
• He maintained that the underlying commercial decision was sound and that a difficult decision of this kind 
was never going to please everyone, whichever way it was made. 
• On direct questioning, it was confirmed that no discount was offered to supporters relocating to the 
Patrick's level, only pricing described as “like for like” against the prior year, which, combined with this 
year's general price increase, has resulted in a real-terms rise for some of those supporters. 
• The CEO accepted this specific point, saying that holding last year's price for those moved to Patrick's, to 
reflect the inconvenience, “has been a fair point” and something the club should look at. 
FAB Members estimated a meaningful minority of the roughly 30 supporters affected are seriously unhappy, 
though it was also noted that several affected fans have accepted the change without complaint, and that one 
vocal supporter's public criticism online had gone further than most others present felt was warranted or fair, 
including comments made privately about club staff that were not aired publicly. The Board agreed those specific 
personal remarks were not for the record. 
Outcome: no change was agreed at the meeting. The Club acknowledged fair criticism around the lack of a 
Patrick's-level discount and agreed to look at whether some form of price protection could still be offered. The 
CEO committed to bringing comparable decisions to the FAB in future where practical. 
8. Community Trust Funding — Update 
PH gave an update, alongside the Chair and RH, on a meeting held three to four weeks earlier with the 
Community Trust regarding new funding. This will support a series of themed matchday events, planned around 
EFL calendar dates and kept deliberately low-key: a launch event, the Stevenage game on 5 September, a home-
debut takeover event around the Mansfield game in March, Inclusive Reds in December, a Rainbow Reds 
Takeover Day, a Reminiscent Reds Takeover Day (a scheme PH personally volunteers with) and a Community 
Trust Takeover Day. 
The CEO raised concern that this amounted to several separate takeover days and questioned whether that was 
too much to deliver well. PH and JB explained how the events would be delivered in practice: positioned around 
the from of the stadium and the Ozone area and run without requiring large additional staffing, on the basis that 
a smaller number of well-run events is preferable to overstretching. 
9. Ozone 
A question was raised about when the Ozone would be available again for regular use, including the weekly 
Reminiscent Reds sessions. Club staff confirmed there is a reason for the current unavailability but said the detail 
was not appropriate to share in open session. CEO said for PH to pick it up with the Head of the Community. 
10. 2027 
The Chair and PH reported on an initial meeting with Darren Hayes to discuss ideas for 2027, which marks both 
the Club's anniversary (the Club is believed to have formed in 1887, with a first organisational meeting the 
previous year) and the anniversary of the 1997 Premier League season. A Working Group is being formed, and 
the Club is actively seeking FAB Members and other Volunteers to support it, alongside Darren and Nicky Eaden 
from the club side. 
The CEO stressed that staff capacity is currently very limited, and that anything taken on for the anniversary will 
need to come from somewhere, so Fan Volunteers leading elements of the celebration would make a real 
difference. A supporter, Liam Dyson, was suggested by DW as a potential contact for the working group, on the 
strength of his work on Day Dream Believers, the film about the club's promotion to the Premier League. 
11. Any Other Business 
New Ticket Office - layout and accessibility. MW raised the layout of the new ticket office, specifically whether 
the lower, accessible counter is clearly marked, since he is not able to see it himself. JB agreed this needed a 
clear sign and said he would look at it with a colleague. He confirmed a recent access audit has been carried out 
and said the Club would look at options for a priority queuing system for disabled supporters on matchdays. 
Disabled supporter passport cards. MW raised feedback that the current cards are too large and carry too much 
printed information. JB agreed to look at a smaller, redesigned version during the next print run. 
Reasonable adjustments at the Ticket Office. MW also asked whether access needs could be recorded once 
against a season ticket rather than explained afresh each visit. JB said this depends on the specific adjustment 
needed but agreed the principle of a supporter being able to flag their needs to a Steward, without repeated 
explanation, was worth looking at. 
Watching matches abroad. CC on asked whether she would be able to watch matches on iFollow while abroad, 
having struggled to do so previously. Lewis Robinson, joining by phone, confirmed league games are available on 
video abroad (audio only for supporters watching from inside the UK for those fixtures shown on Sky), but that 
Carabao Cup and FA Cup matches cannot be shown on video outside the UK under broadcast restrictions; audio 
commentary only. He confirmed access is determined by the location of the supporter's device, not by VPN use. 
Matchday broadcast and hosting changes. Lewis Robinson also confirmed staffing changes for matchday 
broadcast and hospitality hosting, following the departure of a previous host, Jason. Callum Cooper will take on 
hosting the hospitality lounges before kick-off and will provide iFollow commentary during the match. A newly 
recruited Stadium Announcer, will be in place at Saturday's game, He will handle pitch-side announcements 
before, during and after matches. All Club video and audio streaming, including commentary, will be available 
through the Club's app. 
Fan advisory guidance comparison. 
Following on from item 3, PG presented his own detailed comparison between the final published guidance and 
the earlier provisional version, confirming the Club's early impression that little of substance had changed: 
• The term “Fan Advisory Board” has been replaced in the guidance with “Supporter Fan Representatives”. 
• The requirement for fan sign-off of a club's annual report has been softened; it is now encouraged rather 
than mandatory. 
• The reporting deadline for that document has moved from 1 June to 15 August. 
• Term limits for elected Fan Representatives are now specified: three-year terms, with a maximum of three 
terms, matching Barnsley's existing arrangements. 
• The heritage duty section has been expanded from a footnote to a full chapter, and annual declarations 
and discretionary licence conditions are now standalone chapters. 
• The core principles, democratic, independent, fair and proportional fan consultation, remain broadly 
unchanged. 
No action was required; this was noted as an information item. 
Fan engagement plan and benchmarking. PG also raised the club's developing fan engagement plan. He and the 
Chair now sit on an EFL-wide Fan Advisory Group, where other clubs, including Reading, Wolves, Lincoln and 
West Ham, have shared their own Fan Engagement Plans. PG suggested Barnsley's plan could be improved by 
taking elements of these other clubs' plans, tied to the Fan Consultation Report the Club will be expected to 
publish under the new IFR framework. 
Board Members discussed how Barnsley's FAB compares with other clubs': relatively few other advisory boards 
meet monthly (Barnsley's does), Wrexham's board meets quarterly, and Reading's process was described, on the 
evidence available to the Board, as more one-way, informing fans rather than holding a genuine two-way 
discussion. The general view in the room was that, while there is always room to improve, Barnsley's process 
compares favourably with the wider EFL picture, and no member disagreed with that assessment. 
Fans' Forum. RH and AB asked whether an in-person fans' forum is planned this year to which the CEO and JB 
said there would be. SB asked if the Chairman would like to join a FAB meeting in the future. The CEO said this 
had been raised at a previous meeting too and that an online format is the more realistic option should the 
chairman be available. 
Membership Scheme. A FAB Member thanked the club for its matchday ticket pricing for the opening fixture 
against Bromley, which prompted JB to highlight the club's £20 membership scheme, which gives £2 off every 
home league matchday ticket, along with other benefits. 
Big Screen. A long-standing supporter request (raised, by one estimate, for around 20 years) for a larger big 
screen was discussed at length. This was prompted partly by comparison with the larger screen at Doncaster 
Rovers' ground. The CEO confirmed the current screen measures roughly 3 metres by 1.75 metres, and that a 
like-for-like upgrade to around 12 metres by 4 metres had been costed at approximately £55,000 to £60,000 all 
in - covering screen, steelwork and software. A new screen would need to remain in its current position due to 
underground cabling and unknown ground conditions preventing an easy move elsewhere. AB suggested a fan-
driven fundraiser, led by the Supporters' Trust, to help fund the upgrade, which prompted discussion of money 
potentially already available in the Trust which it could contribute. 
Views in the room differed on whether Trust funds should be committed to this or held back for contingencies. It 
was agreed in principle that the Trust and the FAB should work more closely together on projects like this. The 
CEO agreed to check the supplier's payment terms to see whether a staged payment plan could make the project 
more achievable. No commitment to proceed was made but this issue will be raised again. 
St Peter's Church Plaque. The Chair reported that Barnsley Museum, working with The Reverend Blair at St 
Peter's Church, has commissioned a plaque in memory of Reverend Tiverton Preedy, recognised as the club's 
founder, with a possible link to regional media coverage. The unveiling, originally expected in October, may be 
delayed. All FAB Members are invited. It was agreed to ask Barnsley Museum whether the event could be timed 
to align with the 2027 anniversary celebrations, and to pass on contact details for the volunteer, Neil Richardson, 
who travels to London each year to tend to Reverend Preedy's grave, so he can be included in the invitation. 
Council Relations. The CEO asked for an update on relations with the newly elected Barnsley Council Leadership. 
The CEO advised that he met them on their fifth day in office. A follow-up meeting is being arranged. Early 
engagement has been positive, with the new administration described as supportive of the football club's role in 
the town. 
Next Meeting. No date was fixed. Given the transfer window closes on 31 August and the demands of the 
opening weeks of the season, the Chair proposed a meeting roughly six weeks out, in mid-September, and asked 
all members to email their availability.

title: FAB Meeting Minutes - 9 June 2026

Barnsley FC Fan Advisory Board | Meeting of Tuesday 9 June 2026

Barnsley FC Fan Advisory Board 
Meeting Minutes, Tuesday 9 June 2026 
Held online via Microsoft Teams. 
1. Attendees 
Present 
• Steve Brain, Chair of the FAB 
• Phil Hall, FAB Member 
• Claire Calton, FAB Member 
• Martin Wilson, FAB Member (joined late) 
• Dominic Wood, FAB Member (joined late, returning from travel) 
• Paul Gallagher, FAB Member 
• Jon Flatman, Chief Executive Officer, Barnsley FC 
• John Bird, Head of Ticketing and Fan Engagement, Barnsley FC 
Apologies 
• Robin Harris, last-minute work commitment, sent advance notice. 
Quorum 
The full board, bar one apology, was in attendance, so the meeting was quorate and 
proceeded. The Chair noted he had to leave by 8pm, so members agreed to work through 
the agenda efficiently. 
2. Minutes of the Previous Meeting and Matters Arising 
No formal approval of the previous minutes was recorded at this meeting. Several matters 
arising from earlier meetings were carried into the agenda and Any Other Business, 
including the recurring question about hotel discounts for travelling supporters and ongoing 
stadium project works. 
The Chair opened by congratulating JF on bringing Daniel back into the club. 
3. FAB Structure, Vacancies and Communications 
The Chair reported that he believed the Board's current term is up this year. (This was 
clarified later - see below) and that four vacancies had been advertised on the fan message 
board (BBS). 
Only one response had been received: from a lifelong supporter, Peter Harrison, who lives in 
Bedford. Pete has worked in construction at a senior level and is now retired and keen to 
volunteer his time. (His brother is Mike Harrison, the former England rugby union captain.) 
The Chair felt he would be a strong addition and proposed introducing him to the board by 
way of a Teams call. 
PG questioned the wider plan given the Board's term being up and argued that any 
vacancies should be advertised more widely than just the fan message board. 
JF advised holding off on advertising the vacancies more widely for now. His reasoning was 
that the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) is due to publish guidance shortly on the 
future of Fan Advisory Boards and fan engagement at clubs. That guidance would set out 
expectations on structure, how often meetings should be held, and a legal framework to

work from. JF stressed it would be "fit for purpose rather than a prescription” but would give 
the FAB firmer ground to stand on when going out to the fan base. 
JB added that he had been on a call with the IFR specifically about fan engagement, where 
he explained what our FAB does. The IFR indicated they would publish information on fan 
engagement in the coming months, after which the FAB would have a clearer picture. The 
IFR will not consult with individual FABs until the back end of the year because they are 
stretched across all clubs, but they are happy to attend a future FAB meeting when invited. 
CC asked what happens at the end of a member's term if no one comes forward to fill the 
position. DW recalled from the original memorandum of understanding that members were 
eligible for two terms. JB, reading from the terms of reference, confirmed the initial term is 
two years, with provision from 2026 onwards for up to three terms. JF explained that the 
articles could be changed if needed, but that consistency points to roughly three terms; 
serving four or more would start to look like an ownership situation. He noted the BFC FAB 
is not at that point yet. 
Outcome: The board agreed to hold off on advertising the vacancies more widely until the 
IFR's July guidance is published. Pete Harrison would still be brought in, for continuity and to 
bolster numbers. PG volunteered to join the Chair on an introductory call with him. 
4. Season Ticket Sales 
JB reported strong season ticket sales. Tickets went on sale later than last year but were 
running at more than double the equivalent point twelve months ago and had been above 
last year's figures from week one. 
JF confirmed season tickets are up on last year despite a price increase., He said the Club 
was delighted with the campaign, particularly given the season just gone. The Club typically 
sells around 900 season tickets after the early-bird deadline, so there was still work to do, 
but the early signs were very positive. 
JF noted the club had spent less on “paid-for” marketing this year and leaned more on social 
media, though he cautioned that every season is different and sales are influenced by many 
factors. He congratulated JB and his team on the campaign, saying it could only be seen as 
a success. 
5. Independent Football Regulator (IFR) Update 
JF gave an update on the IFR, which is coming into statute. Key points: 
• The IFR is fundamentally a risk assessor; there to assess the long-term sustainability 
of clubs. 
• A significant amount of work is going into transparency around ownership, including a 
public record of who owners are and their holdings. 
• The Owners' and Directors' test now sits with the IFR: any new appointment into 
ownership or a directorship has to be approved by them. 
• Changes this month require approval for alterations to a club's crest, protecting 
heritage. 
• Where a club's finances are deemed a risk, the IFR could in principle request that the 
club put up a bond. This has been raised at other clubs and is relevant context for 
supporters. 
• Wider work includes the State of the Game report and connected debates about a 
fairer financial distribution across the EFL and Premier League. 
JF said met with David Cogan of the IFR and found him very open and transparent. JB 
added that, on his fan-engagement call with the IFR, they were happy with what Barnsley 
are doing, saw no issues, and would come to a future meeting.

Minutes | 9 June 2026 | Page 3 of 6 
6. Cost Control (SCMP) and Player Trading 
JF explained changes to the cost control rules (the Salary Cost Management Protocol, or 
SCMP), which came through last month and will be voted on by clubs. The headline change 
is that the contribution clubs can count is now straight equity at 50%, replacing the previous 
tapered arrangement (members referenced an earlier 60% figure). The aim is to reduce club 
losses and make clubs more sustainable, which links directly back to the IFR's purpose. 
PG asked whether the change went far enough and whether there had been discussion of 
going further. Jon said views had varied: some clubs would have gone further, others not as 
far, and the agreed position was a compromise that could command a vote. He explained 
that the cost of recruitment is already biting, using the phrase that "a quid now costs you two 
quid", and that the full effect would not be seen until the end of next season. 
The discussion moved on to player trading. JF explained that player sales become a more 
important and reliable way to generate revenue to invest into football spend, and that selling 
one player can be worth roughly the same as doubling season ticket revenue. MW and DW 
pressed on what this means for Barnsley's recruitment and the need to sell to survive. Jon 
agreed the club has to sell, but said it also has to sell well and from a position of strength, 
and that the model of developing players and selling them on remains central. He gave the 
example of a player in the building (referred to as Patrick Kelly) whose value had risen, 
noting that recruitment would look fundamentally different going forward. 
7. Auracast and Audio Commentary for Disabled Supporters 
PH reported back from an RNID hearing loss conference. He explained that Auracast, a 
newer audio-broadcast technology, is developing fast in the UK. All Apple phones and 
earbuds are now Auracast compatible, and there is a push for it to become standard in 
public spaces such as football stadiums and places of worship. PH said it is the coming thing 
and worth the club being aware of early. He knows a contact who could survey the stadium 
and advise exactly what would be needed. 
MW raised the related issue of audio commentary for visually impaired supporters. The 
current Oakwell system is analogue, with a headset and receiver collected from the box 
office. He praised the quality of BFC commentary and the experience at other clubs and 
made the point that the commentator's quality matters as much as the equipment. JF agreed 
there are two separate questions: the quality of the commentary at Oakwell, and how to 
deliver it through better technology. He suggested putting JB in touch with PH’s contact to 
explore options, possibly broadcasting from the disabled box. DW suggested a wired or fibre 
solution as an alternative. 
Outcome: PH to send his contact's details to JB, who will follow up and explore Auracast 
and improved audio commentary provision. 
8. Community Trust Grant 
PH gave a brief update on a grant application connected to the Community Trust, on which 
he has been working with Kieran and James Cook. Around 20% of the funding had been 
approved so far, covering items such as activities for younger children, with a decision on 
the remainder expected before the end of June. 
JF encouraged the board to publicise its involvement to the fan base, pointing out that being 
able to show fans the FAB had input into how money is spent is a clear justification for the 
importance of this FAB. He suggested PH chase the timeline, which he believed was quicker 
than the two weeks Phil had been quoted. PH & SB will pick this up. 
Barnsley FC Fan Advisory Board | Meeting of Tuesday 9 June 2026 
Minutes | 9 June 2026 | Page 4 of 6 
9. EFL FAB Network 
The Chair reported on the new English Football League FAB Network, an initiative bringing 
together fan groups from an estimated 25 to 30 EFL clubs. The inaugural meeting had been 
held online the week before, with the aim of building a national network and taking views on 
structure. The Chair gave the meeting a verbal account of Barnsley's FAB issues and 
challenges, emphasising the positive relationship it has with the Club. 
Ticketing came up as the main challenge across several clubs. The Chair noted a range of 
experiences from the various club attendees, ranging from very poor to excellent. 
In summary the view was that we should continue to attend, as it will give our FAB the 
opportunity to tap into best practice and avoid pitfalls experienced by other FABs across the 
EFL. 
JF welcomed the initiative but cautioned against it becoming a "war stories" or self-help 
group where the most pessimistic voices dominate. He encouraged a focus on best practice, 
learning: “who is doing things well and how”, rather than airing grievances. The Chair agreed 
and confirmed the first meeting had not in fact been dominated by complaints. 
Outcome: The Chair to continue attending the network meetings. Continuity was felt to be 
valuable, but any FAB member could attend, including as an observer. PG advised that he 
would like to attend the next meeting. 
10. Play-off Final Anniversary 
The FAB discussed the anniversary of the play-off final at Cardiff and the related memories 
and content appearing on the club website. JF asked whether the FAB could lead on some 
of the commemoration. The Chair confirmed the FAB was happy to help, and PH raised the 
issue of looking ahead to next year. JF suggested speaking to Darren Hayes at the club to 
coordinate, with the FAB providing manpower and the club getting behind it. 
Outcome: PH and the Chair to speak to Daz about the FAB taking on some of the 
anniversary content and activity. 
11. Any Other Business 
The Chair worked through a list of points raised by supporters via the fan message board 
and other channels. 
Hotel discounts for travelling supporters. A supporter had again asked whether discounts 
were available for fans travelling from a distance who wanted to stay overnight. John Bird 
confirmed the club now has a deal in place offering 10% off a stay, with the information 
provided to away supporters. He would share the details and look to push it further. 
Sanitary bins and products. A supporter had asked why there were not sanitary bins in all 
toilets, a point PH echoed. JB confirmed Barnsley were one of the first clubs to provide free 
sanitary products and are looking to reintroduce them. On bins, he and the Head of HR had 
walked round all the toilets to assess how many were needed; some toilets had bins and 
some did not, notices had been put up, and provision is being increased for next season. CC 
suggested also placing bins outside the toilets so that supporters who cannot get into a 
cubicle at half-time are catered for and welcomed the progress. 
Paul Conway. The Chair asked whether former owner Paul Conway had been pursued by 
the club for any mismanagement. Jon Flatman indicated there was nothing to add: enough 
had been said, the relevant documentation between the parties and the EFL was a matter of 
record, and everything public is public. No further action was indicated. 
Website and social media accuracy. The Chair raised inaccuracies in club website 
notifications and social media posts and asked what the checking process is. The trigger had

been the pre-season friendlies announcement, which carried confusing fixture dates. PH 
added an example of an incorrect match-result post. JF explained that errors happen at 
every club and even on major outlets, and that a full proofreading layer would roughly double 
the staff needed, for limited benefit. He drew a clear distinction, however: minor typos are 
one thing, but getting a fixture date wrong is a serious error the club should get right. On the 
Scarborough kick-off time specifically, JB clarified that Barnsley had it correct at 1pm; the 
discrepancy was on Scarborough's side. PG suggested using a tool to catch spelling and

Hand dryers. The Chair asked whether all hand dryers in the toilets are working, noting it

publication and to ensure it is presented as a summary rather than a full podcast of the

Stadium projects. PG asked for an update on outstanding stadium projects, including the

title: FAB Meeting Minutes - 26 March 2026
content_text:
• FAB Meeting 
• Date: 26 March 2026 
• Location: Online (Teams) 
• Attendees: Steve Brain, Jon Flatman, Phil Hall, Martin Wilson, John Bird, Claire 
Calton 
• Apologies: Robin Harris, Dominic Wood, Paul Gallagher. 
Agenda Items and Discussion 
1. Previous Minutes 
Steve opened by noting the prompt circulation of previous minutes and set expectations 
for similar timeliness. No objections were raised. 
2. Club Accounts and Financial Position 
Jon presented a detailed summary of the club’s accounts up to June 2025. 
Key points included: 
• - Revenue increased by £1.3m (15%), mainly due to a new Sky broadcast deal, 
improved commercial activity, and a strong cup run. 
• - Operating costs fell by £2m, but this was partly due to the previous year being a 
13-month period. 
• - Wages rose by £1m (like-for-like), driven by first team player costs. 
• - Player trading profits were significantly lower than the previous year, resulting in 
a total loss of £6.5m. 
• - The club’s bank balance was maintained through £5.3m in owner equity and 
£4.9m from prior player sales. 
Jon highlighted the broader context: average League One losses have risen sharply, with 
owner funding now averaging £9m per club. He described the situation as 
unsustainable. warning that the "arms race" in player spending is putting clubs at risk. 
The club’s position is not out of line with the division, but the overall trend is concerning. 
Fan representatives acknowledged the gravity of the situation, with Steve and others 
expressing concern about owner fatigue and the risk of owners walking away. 
3. League-wide Financial Crisis and Regulatory Response 
Jon explained ongoing efforts at league level to address escalating costs, including 
discussions around tighter spending rules and a fairer distribution of Premier League 
money. He noted that a new independent football regulator (IFR) is being established, 
which will require clubs to demonstrate financial resilience and fan engagement to 
obtain a licence. 
There was debate about whether clubs can realistically control wage inflation without 
collective action. Jon was candid about the lack of easy solutions, emphasising the 
need for unity across clubs and warning that first movers in cost control risk competitive 
disadvantage. 
4. Season Ticket Pricing and Benefits 
John Bird outlined proposed season ticket pricing: 
• - Average increase of 6% for adults and concessions, equating to £20–£30 per 
adult and £10–£20 per concession. 
• - Matchday prices to rise by £2, with a new “A star” category for high-profile 
games. 
• - Flexi ticket options to be reviewed, with possible removal of the 15-game option 
due to low uptake. 
• - Additional benefits for season ticket holders, including prize draws, mascot 
packages, hospitality upgrades, and discounts on coach travel. 
Fan reps queried the impact of price rises and the effectiveness of flexi tickets. John and 
Jon acknowledged that sales depend on multiple factors, including team performance, 
and agreed to continue refining the offer. 
5. Communication and Supporter Sentiment 
There was discussion of a recent interview with Conor Hourihane, which had not been 
well received by fans. Jon said he was aware of the negative reaction and would address 
it in due course. 
Steve and others stressed the importance of clear, honest communication, especially 
around difficult decisions. Jon agreed, noting that upcoming club communications 
would aim to explain the financial realities and the rationale behind decisions. 
6. Protest Incident 
The group discussed the recent tennis ball protest. Jon confirmed that those identified 
had been invited in for meetings and had their tickets suspended pending review. He 
was firm that such actions are criminal offences and cannot be tolerated, though he 
recognised the right to protest. Most fan reps felt the protest was embarrassing and 
counterproductive. 
7. Stewarding and Matchday Searches 
Concerns were raised about the manner of security searches at recent matches, with 
some fans finding staff abrupt or accusatory. Jon acknowledged the feedback, 
explained that increased searches followed the protest incident, and committed to 
ongoing review with the security provider. He noted that most stewards do a good job 
but accepted that improvements could be made. 
8. Pre-season Events and Anniversaries 
Jon and John Bird mentioned plans for pre-season events at Oakwell, including possible 
World Cup-related activities and concerts, though details were not confirmed. Martin 
asked about marking the anniversaries of the 2006 and 2016 promotion teams; Jon said 
the commercial team had plans in hand. 
9. Community Trust and Premier League Funding 
Phil and Steve reported on a meeting with the Community Trust regarding a funding 
application for community projects, including outreach to LGBT and ethnic minority 
groups. The Trust is seeking a 20% increase in Premier League funding, and FAB input 
was provided. 
10. Supporters Trust and FAB Vacancies 
There was discussion about the relaunch of the Supporters Trust and the overlap with 
FAB. Jon suggested joint events and communications to avoid confusion. The group 
agreed to keep vacancies under review, pending further guidance from the Regulator. 
11. Audio Descriptive Commentary 
Martin raised the issue of audio descriptive commentary for visually impaired and 
autistic supporters, particularly at away matches. He is liaising with Cambridge United 
and offered to share best practice with other clubs. 
Actions 
• Jon to confirm whether the accounts summary can be published. (New) 
• John Bird and Jon to finalise season ticket benefits and communicate details. 
(Ongoing) 
• Club to review stewarding and security feedback with FGH. (Ongoing) 
• Jon to prepare and issue a club statement addressing recent issues and financial 
context. (New) 
• Darren (commercial) to progress plans for anniversary events. (Ongoing) 
• Phil and Steve to maintain dialogue with Community Trust regarding funding 
application. (Ongoing) 
• Martin to liaise with Cambridge United and share audio commentary best 
practice. (Ongoing) 
• FAB to monitor Supporters Trust relaunch and consider joint events. (Ongoing)

title: FAB Meeting Minutes - 12 February 2026
content_text:
BFC FAB Meeting 12/02/26 
Microsoft Teams 
Meeting start time: 17.55 
Meeting end time: 20.12 
1. Attendees 
Name Role Representation 
Jon Flatman CEO, Barnsley FC Club staff 
John Bird Head of Ticketing and Fan Engagement Club staff 
Paul Gallagher FAB Member Supporter representative 
Steve Brain FAB Chair / FAB Member Supporter representative 
Martin Wilson FAB Member Supporter representative 
Claire Calton FAB Member Supporter representative 
Apologies 
Dominic Wood, Phil Hall, Robin Harris, 
Agenda 
1. Previous Minutes and Actions. 
2. Season Tickets. 
3. Football Governance Bill 
4. Road Closures, Anti Terrorism. 
5. FAB Re-set: 
o Comms 
o Social Media Presence 
o Fans' Questions 
o FAB Vacancies 
6. Weston Park Raffle. 
7. In ground Commentary. 
8. AOB 
9. Next Meeting. 
1. Minutes of the meeting 
Previous Minutes agreed and published on Club Website with no objections raised. 
SB advised that the meeting was not quorate but that the meeting would proceed with 
minutes taken on a discussion basis only. 
2. Season Tickets (JF) 
Areas covered: renewal strategy, pricing pressure, incentives, revenue modelling and 
supporter expectations. 
Rising costs and financial background 
• JF outlined significant cost pressures: 
o National Insurance increases. 
o Minimum wage increases affecting casual staff. 
o Rising utilities and product costs. 
o Player wages increasing by on average around 13 percent year on year 
within the season across non promoted or related League 1 clubs. 
o Season ticket income reportedly around £1.5m net. 
o VAT removes 20% of any increase. 
• JF emphasised the importance of season ticket revenue in sustaining the club 
and supporting squad competitiveness. 
Attendance obstacles 
• Fewer Saturday games. 
• Increased midweek fixtures. 
• Weather. 
• Televised matches affecting walk up numbers. 
• Importance of on pitch performance to attendees 
• Examples of low attendance, such as the recent Tuesday match v Northampton. 
Price increases 
• JF indicated initial modelling of an increase was underway but subject to board 
approval. 
• Club is undertaking L1 comparisons especially those who have released 26/27 
prices. 
• CC referenced seeing data suggesting Barnsley were already among the lowest 
priced. 
Alternative ticketing options 
Multiple ideas were raised by FAB members, with JF welcoming innovation: 
a) Attendance incentive 
• PG proposed a 100 percent attendance reward (rebate, voucher or similar), 
stressing that incentives should reward attendance rather than penalise 
absences. 
b) Flexi ticketing 
• PG and others suggested the flexi ticket had not been priced attractively enough. 
• JB confirmed previous sales levels and difficulties in pricing between: 
o Early bird season ticket 
o Matchday prices 
o A meaningful flexi price 
• JF noted limited margin between matchday and season ticket pricing leaves little 
space for flexi products and that Season tickets should always be the lowest 
price. 
c) Variable pricing / “hot ticket” models 
• JF referenced examples used in US sports where pricing changes by block 
occupancy. 
• Challenges with seat migration identified, citing difficulties policing people 
relocating to higher value seats. 
d) Midweek incentives 
• CC proposed low cost gestures like a free hot drink on very cold nights, 
especially for children. 
• JF agreed in principle and asked the ticketing team to model the cost based on 
50 to 75 percent uptake. 
e) Youth incentives 
• Discussion around rewards for children attending all matches. 
• CC suggested prizes such as meeting a favourite player or attending a training 
session. 
• JF supported the idea and stressed all prizes must be realistic to obtain and not 
limited to one or two winners. 
f) Marketing and payment models 
• PG raised subscription style framing. 
• JB confirmed existing four, six and ten month finance options via V12 Finance. 
• JF explained: 
o In house subscription models cause severe cash flow problems. 
o Finance house solutions avoid cash flow issues but include set up costs. 
o Marketing could position the ten month plan as “£X per month” . 
o Club must comply with financial regulatory constraints. 
g) Transfer window discussion relevant to season ticket messaging 
• Several questions later in the meeting touched on: 
o January window activity. 
o Need to invest transfer funds wisely. 
o Ensuring fans believe in the squad direction. 
(Detailed notes appear later under FAB Re set / Fans’ Questions.) 
Outcome: 
• Extensive exploratory discussion. 
• No decisions taken due to non quorum. 
• General agreement that: 
o Incentives will be explored. 
o Flexi ticket pricing will be reviewed. 
o Marketing and subscription framing will be strengthened. 
Actions: See Action Log. 
3. Football Governance Bill / FAB (JF) 
JF gave a substantial, detailed briefing on the new Independent Football Regulator (IFR) 
legislation. 
Discussion Detail: 
Overview of regulatory framework 
• The IFR Act introduces a mandatory licensing regime across all leagues from 
Premier League to National League. 
• Licensing criteria include fan engagement, financial sustainability, ownership 
structures and risk management. 
• Fan engagement is one of five statutory areas where clubs must demonstrate 
compliance. 
FAB structure and requirements 
• Fan representatives must be democratically elected or clearly justified 
representatives (eg. supporters groups). 
• Clubs cannot handpick members without justification. 
• Hybrid models (elected plus appointed for marginalised groups) are allowed. 
• The regulator can request justification for every FAB member. 
• FAB meetings, agendas, minutes and governance will form part of a club’s 
licence evidence. 
• JF stated Barnsley FC is already ahead of many clubs, having operated FAB 
meetings for a year. 
Timeline 
• First consultation complete. 
• Final regulatory framework expected in March. 
• FAB structure and elections may need to be reviewed after March. 
Reporting and compliance 
• IFR is expected to be “light touch” for well run clubs but intrusive for high risk 
clubs. 
• FAB must demonstrate transparency but commercial confidentiality still applies. 
Outcome: 
• JF advised that FAB members should read the full 50 plus page consultation 
document. 
• JF to provide the document. 
• Further structural decisions deferred until the final March IFR publication. 
Actions: See Action Log. 
Risks / Concerns: 
• Any FAB composition changes made now may have to be reversed post March. 
• Need to ensure accessibility of documents for visually impaired members. 
4. Road Closures and Anti Terrorism (JF) 
Context: 
Anti terrorism threat level for sports grounds remains “substantial” . National guidance 
emphasises risks from vehicle attacks. 
Discussion Detail: 
• South Yorkshire Police have written to Barnsley Council requesting a rapid review 
of road closures around Oakwell. 
• Desktop assessment suggests an extension to closures beyond Grove Street, 
including the three roads up the hill. 
• JF stated the club is pushing back, seeking evidence of risks considered before 
changes are imposed. 
• Any changes would affect vehicle access only. 
• Residents also impacted. 
• FAB minutes must word the issue carefully to avoid premature conclusions. 
Outcome: 
• Club to continue discussions with police, council and traffic management 
company. 
• FAB to await further information. 
Actions: See Action Log. 
Risks / Concerns: 
• Supporter disruption. 
• Resident impact. 
• Potential for misinterpretation if communicated poorly. 
• Additional matchday costs to the club 
5. FAB Re-set (PG / All) 
Sub items: Comms, Minutes, Social Media, Fans’ Questions, FAB Vacancies 
(a) Comms and Minutes 
• All recognised the problems the Group has had with minutes and minutes 
approval since FAB inception; creating a poor impression for those fans keen to 
see quick and meaningful communication. The use of co-pilot will help improve 
this area. 
(b) Social Media Presence 
• Not substantively discussed beyond general concern about communication 
reach. 
(c) Fans’ Questions 
The meeting noted a very large volume of supporter questions submitted via PG. Due to 
time constraints and the long discussion on the regulator, JF cautioned against deferring 
everything to writing, as this may be perceived as avoidance and to ensure two way 
communication. JF was happy to answer all questions verbally and pick up additional 
items in writing. 
The group recognised the importance of this and agreed to address as many questions 
as possible in the remaining time available in the meeting. Any questions not covered 
will be submitted to the Club in writing by PG/SB. The Club will respond asap. 
Below are the questions discussed verbally during the meeting: 
Topics Discussed Verbally 
Fan Forum recording not published 
• JF advised that there had been technical difficulties on the night with some 
footage being corrupted. This related to around 20 minutes prior to the interval. 
• Independent journalists and FAB members were present so the content is 
already public. 
• Club will publish remaining footage but accepted criticism unavoidable. 
January transfer window 
• JF provided a detailed summary: 
o Approximately 20 transactions. 
o Defensive reinforcement was a priority due to goals conceded. 
o New goalkeeper brought in early. 
o Experienced centre half signed as free agent to avoid deadline day 
dependency and to ensure early Jan arrival. 
o Striker succession planning explained. 
o DKD sale: Jon emphasised the club must show a pathway for players 
upon recruitment and when the right price is on offer, the club will 
consider these seriously. Uniqueness of the late offer from Wrexham and 
the opportunity for use of funds in a 'better buyers market' in the summer. 
o Scott Banks (loan) has been a valuable addition and Charlie Lennon 
(permanent) has high potential for the future. 
o Loan and permanent markets considered at all times. 
o Importance of the balance between young inexperienced but talented 
younger 'asset' players and of older more experienced players. 
o Difficult historic recruitment window of January due to being in season 
and always subject to change. eg Jacob Brown was diverted to 
Portsmouth on the final day of window. 
o Full and wider engagement of more people internally within the 
recruitment process. 
o Build upon the permanent recruitment of young talent BFC has in the 
building and grow that as a focus each window. 
o Leo Farrell as an example of an academy youngster who may well benefit 
from an opportunity. 
DKD Transfer fee 
• JF outlined that all transfer values and contingencies (additional payments) are 
undisclosed at all clubs in recent times. BFC is no different in that respect. 
• JF stated value would be visible in accounts. 
• JF challenged assumptions about FAB members valuations for a 28 year old 
League One player. 
Fan Zone 
• Club has paused progress due to Christmas fixture congestion and January 
transfer window workload. 
• To resume exploration of alternatives shortly. 
• Possibility that improving concourses may offer better return than a small scale 
Fan Zone but all options will be considered. 
• Licence restrictions limit non matchday usage which reduce viability of a larger 
fan zone. 
Electronic advertising boards 
• JF confirmed rental was c. £80k to £90k per year, purchase over £350k plus 
software and operating. 
• No commercial justification at present due to low broadcast audience in League 
One. 
• Would consider if a major sponsor required them as additional investment would 
offset with revenue. 
Weekly lottery publication 
• Commitment given to publish weekly where possible. 
• Staff absences can delay posting but draws always occur.

1. Minutes and feedback from last meeting 
The group reviewed the September minutes, which were published and circulated. 
Some members felt that October’s informal notes should be published for 
transparency, but others argued they lacked sufficient detail and could cause 
confusion. Consensus was to retain October notes internally, with a commitment 
to improve minute-taking for future meetings. 
SB 
2. Confirmation & Communication of FAB changes 
 The resignation of Kelly Drury was formally acknowledged, with the FAB 
expressing gratitude for her contributions. Steve Brain was confirmed as Chair. The 
FAB and the Club agreed to issue a statement and video regarding the changes., 
but there was debate about the tone—whether it should be formal or more 
personal to foster engagement. 
SB 
3. FAB momentum 
The FAB highlighted concerns about its visibility and impact, noting 
that previous initiatives had not gained traction. Paul Gallagher advocated for a 
stronger social media presence, while others cautioned against relying solely on 
digital engagement, stressing the importance of face-to-face interaction. The club 
suggested a pre-match FAB presence, which was widely supported. 
SB/JF/PG 
4. Fan Engagement/FAB evening with guests 
Plans for a fan engagement event before Christmas were discussed. Steve Brain 
favoured a standalone FAB event to build identity, but others, including Jon 
Flatman, argued that joint events with the Club would attract more attendees and 
media coverage. There was debate about the format—whether to focus on 
informal Q&A or structured panels—and concerns about balancing inclusivity with 
logistical constraints. 
Further discussion on this will take place. 
SB/JF 
5. Field of Vision 
John Bird explained the Field of Vision device for visually impaired fans, costing 
£625 per season. The device uses tactile vibrations to indicate ball position and 
possession, with an operator required to track match events via laptop. Members 
praised the initiative’s inclusivity, but raised concerns about recruiting and training 
Operators, and whether the technology would be reliable in a busy stadium 
environment. The Club committed to funding and piloting the device, with a review 
after launch. 
JB/SB 
6. EFL Sticker Swap Shop

Claire Carlton proposed Panini sticker swap sessions at home games, starting with 
the Leyton Orient match. Members supported the idea, noting its potential to 
engage younger fans. Some cautioned about safeguarding and supervision, 
suggesting that volunteers be recruited to oversee swaps. John Bird agreed to 
promote the initiative in match-day communications and ensure appropriate 
oversight. 
CC/JB

The club reported 2,400 responses to the EDI survey (78% male, 22% female). Phil 
Hall questioned whether the survey reached underrepresented groups and 
suggested targeted outreach. The Club agreed to analyse the data and compare 
census benchmarks, but acknowledged that further work was needed to address 
gaps. There was consensus that the EDI Code of Practice should be 
widely publicised and regularly reviewed. 
PH/JB 
8. Group Bookings 
The Club are planning a discounted ticket scheme for groups of 15+ at £15 per 
adult. Paul Gallagher highlighted the potential for engaging London-based 
supporters, while Claire Carlton suggested leveraging grassroots networks. Some 
members raised concerns about the impact on season ticket holders. The Club 
responded that group sales are standard in other sports and can boost attendance 
but agreed to monitor feedback. 
JB/PG

Steve Brain described the Visual History project, and advised that Julian Germain, 
the Author would be happy to attend the next FAB meeting.

sponsor. Julian will present at a future FAB meeting, with the launch pushed to next

Agenda Item 1 - January Transfer Window 
Whilst it was recognised that inviting MS to the FAB meeting was an unusual 
request, it is to the Club’s and MS’s credit that they facilitated that opportunity. 
The overwhelming concern of Barnsley Fans at the end of the January transfer 
window was to look for some sort of explanation as to what the Club’s approach 
and thinking was during the month. The FAB exists to represent fellow supporters 
and it was felt that we would have been doing our fellow supporters a disservice to 
not at least try and broker a meeting and engage with the Club. 
The output from this meeting is detailed below. 
The meeting was a two-way dialogue, with questions and answers throughout. 
Mladen gave an initial overview of the process, after which queries were raised 
by the FAB members, to establish the following: 
● There are a number of individuals involved in the recruitment process at 
the club: The Board, The Head Coach and the Recruitment Team. 
● It is not just data driven recruitment; players are watched both internally 
and external to the club. 
● This is how a vast majority of the clubs operate from mid Championship to 
League two clubs. 
● Once the January transfer window closes, the club begin to review the 
team’s current situation, identify the team’s needs in more detail, 
narrowing this down and being more specific, and then start to identify any 
potential targets from other clubs. 
● In recent years we have lost the services of Herbie Kane and Devante Cole, 
and therefore, the focus was for players that were ready to start. 
● This monitoring continues throughout the season for players both internal 
and external to the club. 
● Prior to the summer, a list of desirable players to approach is formulated 
over the summer months. This is then presented to the Stakeholders. 
● These players are then ranked, identifying the Club’s needs and 
expectations. The ranking includes where the potential player is currently, 
their projected ability and their possible progression within a team. 
● Finances are then discussed with the Board regarding the spending budget 
for the future plans and squad. This could be made up of a number of 
elements, including spending per player, how likely is the deal likely to 
2 
come to fruition and what is the timeline available for players and the 
clubs involved. 
● Clubs have different agendas and sometimes this is also a factor in the sale 
or availability of that Club’s under contract players, and their anticipated 
value and what realistic offers could be made. 
● Throughout the summer, from May onwards, the Recruitment Team review 
the list systematically as the target players also have options and choices to 
make. It is not only Barnsley FC in the market looking to buy and sign 
players. 
● The Club may also work and negotiate with a player over a longer period of 
time, considering the longer term prospects for the club. 
● This becomes a balancing act, as we are usually in competition with other 
teams for a small pool of players. 
● Some markets have now been eliminated due to changes in the law for 
European clubs regarding the signing and transferring of players. This has 
had the effect of making the pool for quality players smaller and smaller. 
● We make sure that each position on the field has a potential of 5 players 
who are identified as above average, and then a further 5 who could also 
deliver what we require. 
● All our future targets need to be treated with the strictest confidence, as 
this could alert other clubs to our interest and jeopardize the potential 
opportunity for the transfer to be successful; meaning the best price, 
circumstances and conditions for the club. 
● The longer term sustainability for the club is also vital. These 
considerations include our current players, loan deals in and out of the 
club, and also balancing players' requests and desires to ensure both 
parties remain happy. 
● Loaning out our players also gives the club an opportunity to assist that 
player, to determine whether they (our own younger players) are 
developing as we would hope. 
● Loaning in players gives us the chance to assess a player’s future potential 
and helps us make a judgement on whether we could look at purchasing at 
a future date, 
● Our Recruitment Team is well networked and they continuously feed into 
all the above areas. 
● There is discussion with the Board regarding costs. This incorporates fees 
paid, wages and any potential value that may be interpreted as an “off set” 
of the player’s costs. This is a balance between medium and longer term, 
to ensure risk is calculated and then managed. The Football Club must 
adhere to a number of regulatory bodies in order to continue to operate. 
● Players are not just identified on data. The process may start with data and 
a player may look impressive re his starts and goals ratio for instance. 
Other factors are also analysed, such as his stature, and the league the 
data is formulated from. We also undertake observations of players in 
person through our scouting network, or through recordings and/or media. 
● This is no rule regarding signing under 23s. Signing players, depends 
on the need, availability, current market value and the other factors 
already touched upon. 
● JF referenced the Salary Cost Management Protocol (SCMP) changes for 
next season, which were only voted on by clubs in December; which will 
now only allow a percentage of equity funding by Owners to count as 
income, compared to the current 100% allowance. This will require Owners 
(generally, not just BFC) to invest more funds than they are allowed to use 
for operating purposes under the SCMP rules. Potentially, this incentivised 
3 
other clubs to invest more heavily in January ahead of these rules coming 
in. 
Barnsley FC Community Trust and FAB 
As a separate item, Dave Watson and Kieron Campbell from the BFC Community 
Trust updated the FAB on the work they undertake in the Community. 
It was agreed that the FAB and the BFCCT will strengthen their links and work 
together at every opportunity.

Barnsley FC Fan Advisory Group Meeting Minutes 
Date of Meeting 16th October 2024 
Location Premier Lounge, Oakwell Stadium 
Time 6pm 
Meeting Objective(s) 
Attendance 
Present Apologies 
John Bird - JB Robin Harris - RH Martin Wilson - MW

Steve Brain - SB Claire Calton - CC 
Phil Hall - PH Heather Linney - HL 
Andy Gaskell - AG 
Curtis Ledger - CL
