Agenda, Discussions, Issues 
Topic / Discussion Notes Discussion led by 
1. Welcome KD 
KD welcomed everyone to the meeting. 
2. Previous minutes ALL 
The minutes of the last meeting will be agreed offline. 
3. Updates from previous meetings KD 
a. BFC Accounts KD 
JF will provide an interim financial update in the fan’s forum. Accounts are due out in 
2025 and JF will provide further information at that time. 
PG proposed using a framework, similar to the one discussed by Kieran Maguire from The 
Price of Football, to simplify and explain the club’s financial situation, including who owns 
what percentage of Barnsley FC. PG will gather details for the next meeting. 
b. Man United coach subsidies KD 
KD requested BFC publicise the supporter’s subsidy paid for by BFC 
JB explained that the club subsidised regular supporters’ clubs by giving them £5 per 
person for each fan who travelled with them. However, how this subsidy has been 
managed varies across the different clubs. 
PG noted that most fans might not even be aware of this subsidy. 
c. Charlton Season Ticket offer 
The Charlton “bring a friend” ticket offer received overwhelming praise. 
JB shared that as of now, 522 free upgrades have been claimed by 16/10. 
Overwhelming feeling from all was that it was a great offer 
HL asked how the seating is being sorted out as a specific issue has been raised 
JB – 2 things happening, clubs offering 2 season ticket holders and also free upgrades for 
concessions tickets. The person is trying to upgrade a ticket rather than requesting new 
tickets. Guidance has been put out on the club website. 
The club did look to offer free food outside but were not able to put this in place so 
brought the offers inside. 
HL and PG requested confirmation that enough hot drinks and staffing resources would 
be available to successfully execute the offer. JB assured that arrangements are being 
made. The club is also exploring reconfiguring setups to better support the event. 
d. Tracking Initiatives (sub-discussion) 
HL suggested creating a mid-season and end-of-season summary of various initiatives, 
such as the coach subsidy and other Fan Advisory Board (FAB) suggestions. 
JB confirmed that he is already keeping track of these initiatives. 
e. Reporting Joint Initiatives (sub-discussion) 
DW proposed that BFC and FAB should jointly report these efforts twice a season to 
highlight the work being done. 
JB reminded everyone that the club is also required to report fan engagement efforts to 
the EFL at the end of the season, so this ties in perfectly. 
f. Sky deal - Financial and Attendance Concerns 
DW raised the question of whether the financial support from Sky is essential for the club 
and if Saturday evening games are actually working out in terms of attendance and 
atmosphere. 
PG followed up, asking for clear figures on how much better off the club is under the Sky 
Deal. He noted that Exeter City has suggested their club hasn’t seen significant financial 
benefits from the agreement. 
JB explained that the financial uplift provided by the deal might be negated if supporters 
don’t attend the games which are rescheduled. He emphasized that, while money is 
important, the atmosphere at games is equally critical, especially as it directly impacts 
fan engagement and loyalty. 
 • 
g. Sky deal - season Ticket Sales 
CL highlighted a pressing concern: how the disruption caused by the Sky Deal might 
negatively affect season ticket renewals for the following season. JB acknowledged this, 
sharing that fan comments reflecting this concern are already coming into the club. 
h. Sky Deal - Impact on Traveling Fans 
DW and PG discussed the challenges faced by fans who travel from further afield, such as 
the London Tykes. Previously, these fans had been accommodating of mid-week games, 
but there’s now growing dissatisfaction due to increasing disruptions. 
f. Discussion on Kick-Off Time Adjustments for Midweek Games JB 
JB noted that EFL regulations allow fixtures to kick off between 7:00 PM and 8:05 PM. 
The question posed was whether adjusting the kick-off time, such as moving it to 7:15 
PM, could help bring more fans to midweek games. 
Feedback from FAB members: 
PG: Shared that an earlier kick-off time (e.g., 7:15 PM) wouldn’t make him more likely to 
bring his daughter to a game. In fact, the change could make it harder for him to attend 
personally, especially when traveling from York for work. 
DW: Raised concerns in general about distributing the 100 free tickets Rapid Response 
Telecom give away on a match day. 
DW and PG: Agreed that maintaining the 7:45 PM kick-off time is preferable. 
CL: Highlighted that Friday nights are different from Tuesdays in terms of suitability for 
children attending games. 
General Observations 
JB explained that the Rotherham games timing was non-negotiable. However, there’s 
value in gathering fan feedback on earlier kick-off times for future matches. 
CL emphasized the need for better publicity if earlier kick-off times are introduced. 
4.FAB Meeting structure & IT Structure KD 
Mechanism for Raising Issues 
KD inquired if the current method for bringing issues to the Fan Advisory Board (FAB) is 
working effectively. 
RH mentioned that no feedback has been received via his email inbox so far. 
PG: Suggested that the FAB needs to raise its profile and visibility, particularly through 
social media platforms like TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram. 
CL: Proposed that the FAB should have a physical presence in front of the reception area 
on match days to engage directly with fans. 
PG: Highlighted the need for a noticeable sign to grab people’s attention. 
JB: Suggested leveraging the Ozone system as part of the engagement strategy. 
5. Comms 
Overview/ Website 
The BFC website requires further updates, including the addition of meeting minutes and 
an FAQ section. 
PG emphasized the importance of publishing all meetings on the website, as the current 
setup gives an impression of anonymity. 
PG suggested exploring the creation of a dedicated FAB website or subdomain, such as 
fab.barnsleyfc.co.uk, and it was agreed that PG would investigate this possibility. 
Issue and FAQ Management 
PG: Developed a form and a SharePoint issue tracker in collaboration with SB to triage 
and track issues. This allows even anecdotal submissions to be documented formally 
through the tracker. 
PG also created a FAQ tracker to internally manage FAQs before they are registered on 
the FAB page or website. 
There was a discussion about how this system would function: 
KD: Asked if an auto-reply could be sent to users submitting issues. 
KD: Questioned why a fan would use the form instead of email. 
PG agreed to set up a session to demonstrate how the tracker would work and address 
these concerns. 
Introductory Videos 
RH: Suggested creating introduction videos for the FAB page. 
PG: Stated the need to decide on the key messages for these videos and proposed 
forming a subgroup to manage this. 
It was agreed all members would provide ideas for introductory videos to SB in the first 
instance. 
KD 
6. Match Day Ticket Pricing AG 
JB: Match ticket for this season was set in January when deciding on the season ticket 
pricing for the 2024/25 season. Now reviewing based on Tuesday night attendances. 
There are more offers coming such as ST bring a friend for £10 against Wigan Athletic, 
family ticket prices against Leyton Orient and kids for a quid against Crawley Town. 
7. Flexi tickets for 24/25 season KD 
KD: Are flexi season tickets being considered 
JB: Yes and will be launched shortly. 
8. Promotions for NYD v Wrexham AG 
The group discussed the upcoming Wrexham game on New Year’s Day (NYD) and the 
opportunity to capitalize on their popularity and media coverage, particularly given the 
attention from their high-profile ownership and documentary series. 
Feedback and Ideas 
AG: Suggested using the Wrexham media spotlight to promote tickets, possibly through a 
pricing promotion or special campaign. 
JB: Highlighted that the game is already categorized as a Category A fixture as festive 
fixtures tend to be but noted that games on either side of this date are family-focused 
events, such as “Kids for a Quid.” 
KD: Proposed marketing the town itself to Wrexham fans as part of the game experience 
(similarities with mining communities). 
AG: Suggested exploring a “Welcome to Oakwell” campaign to make the event more 
appealing. 
CL: Proposed creating something unique that could be featured in Wrexham’s 
documentary series, such as a playful theme like “Welshpool vs. Toby Tyke.” 
Next Steps 
AG: Agreed to contact the Wrexham Supporters Trust to discuss potential collaboration or 
involvement. 
ALL: Continued brainstorming potential promotional angles to make the game stand out

PG: Highlighted that offering something for free often leads to a lack of perceived value,

12. Saturday only Season Tickets KD 
KD: Suggested the idea of introducing a Saturday-only season ticket as a potential option 
for fans. 
JB: Responded that this concept doesn’t work for several reasons, citing other clubs 
unsuccessful attempts at implementing a similar option. 
JB mentioned that flexi-tickets could be a more viable solution to meet fan needs. 
The club is currently considering an option for 8-match or 5-match flexi-ticket to be

content_text:
Barnsley FC Fan Advisory Group Meeting Minutes 001 
Date of Meeting Monday 29th January 2024 
Location Legend’s Suite, Oakwell Stadium 
Time 7pm 
Meeting Objective(s) 
Outline the structure of the group and the terms of reference. 
Attendance 
Present Apologies 
Jon Flatman Dominic Wood 
Robert Zuk Michael Sykes 
John Bird Les Elvin 
Cameron Marshall Steve Brain 
Applicants – names available Simon Barraclough 
Agenda, Discussions, Issues 
Topic / Discussion Notes Discussion led by 
1. Introductions 
JF introduced the club employees present to the supporters in attendance. JF 
2. What do we want to achieve? 
Full explanation of what we want to achieve with group. Enabling open communication 
both ways. Not always going to agree on items but having the communication there is 
key. 
JF 
3. Ice breakers 
Group and personal interaction. 
JF/GROUP 
4. Breakout session one - How do you want the group to be formed? 
A discussion in roundtables of terms of reference, meeting frequency, representation and 
chairperson 
GROUP 
5. Feeback from breakout session one 
General feedback points from the groups in no order. 
• We do need a chairperson. Strong person to keep the meetings on agenda. 
• Essential communication channels between the club and the group. 
• Terms of reference required for the group – tight framework for the group. 
• Need an agenda for the meetings as supporters may think it is a free for all. 
• 8-12 people on the committee from different demographics – Supporter groups 
to include but not limited to: Disabled, season ticket holders, match ticket buyers, 
away travellers, different stands, exiled supporters, age, gender. 
• Each committee member will need to be available for supporters to contact them 
for feedback in their area. 
• Formation of sub-groups discussed. 
• Bi-monthly meetings with the committee and the club. 
• Alternate bi-monthly meetings with the wider group. 
• The length of time supporters to be on the committee is TBC. 
• Club to support with admin of the group – minute taking, setup of the meetings. 
• Meetings to take place at Oakwell but could have sessions online too. 
GROUP 
6. Breakout session two – 
A discussion around the 5 key areas for supporters to communicate on at this stage. GROUP 
7. Feedback from breakout session two 
The following issues were raised in no order. 
• Safe standing – where and when? 
• Stewarding at Oakwell 
• Growing the fan base 
• Matchday entertainment – need something to entertain supporters from 
12pm/1pm. Activities pre-match and at half time. 
• Club shop – improvements. 
• Expansion and upgrades to the disabled facilities 
• Understanding the strategic goals of the club 
• Impact of the lease and the length of it 
• Supporter refund for Horsham. 
• Be stronger on the discrimination message to the supporter base. 
• Catering layout in the South Stand 
• Need to get more attendees – how? 
• Travel to and from Oakwell – Car park and road closures. 
• Better communication on why the club makes certain decisions and improved 
response time. 
JF updated the group on Safe Standing and said that this has approval to pursue the 
program of works at board level. Meeting held with SGSA and SAG and two areas have 
been costed. This is under consideration by the board, consultation has started with this 
group and further updates in due course. 
Council Lease provides us investment into the stadium and a permanent Fan Zone is 
being considered. Full board support to proceed to a scheme of works when possible. 
GROUP 
8. AOB 
The club to draft a term of reference for the group to be discussed at the next full 
meeting. 
Skills audit of the members to be sent out and completed by members. 
JF 
9. Close – 9.00pm
